A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaVPR work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable, allowing comparisons across renamed methods and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, fusion and LoRA ablations, dataset statistics, and curation evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds query-length experiments and a qualitative caption-generator comparison.

M1.justification: The four fusion strategies, LLP, LoRA with Multi-Similarity loss, and curation procedure remain unchanged. Renaming cross-modal La- models to LoRA-MS- and expanding their explanations do not establish algorithmic changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GSV-Cities, Pitts30K, Amstertime, and MSLS coverage, including signage, blur, and weather subsets. Query-length sensitivity testing remains within the existing Amstertime text-to-image retrieval task; no new domain or population is documented.

E2.justification: v2 supplementary Figure 7 adds a qualitative comparison between Gemini 2.5 Flash and a generator labelled InternVL 38B inside the figure, but InternCL-38B in its caption. The established retrieval comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 Table 12 adds evaluation conditions with mean query lengths of 15, 25, 35, and 60 words. Existing training schedules and splits remain documented as before. Table 7 also describes the CricaVPR comparator as ViT-L rather than Base, conflicting with the retained Base specification in supplementary Section 4; an actual backbone switch is not established.

E4.justification: v2 adds query-length sensitivity analysis, a qualitative alternative-caption-generator example, and an unquantified report of preliminary mid-fusion degradation. Existing fusion, text-encoder, cleaning, training-strategy, and LoRA ablations are retained, including material moved into the supplement.

E5.justification: Table 12 newly reports query-length dispersion through mean ± standard deviation, alongside minimum and maximum lengths. These statistics describe input variability, not uncertainty in retrieval performance. Neither version reports repeated-run performance uncertainty, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched core table scores remain unchanged. v2 adds length-dependent BLIP results, including LoRA-MS-BLIP R@1 values of 6.5%, 9.0%, 11.0%, and 13.2%. The relationship between the last value and the retained 12.8% main-comparison result is unexplained. Selected R@20 columns and the absolute Pitts30 ADS+LLP results are removed from overview tables.

T1.justification: The fusion definitions, Multi-Similarity objective, LoRA decomposition, and computational-cost approximation are mathematically unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction drops the claim of being the first standardized benchmark and reframes LoRA-MS from a novel strategy to an empirical alignment study. It also removes the universal-regularizer characterization. The principal benchmark, robustness, efficiency, and cross-modal retrieval claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of narrative density and CAT+LLP failure through modality rescaling, and strengthens the catastrophic-forgetting explanation. It emphasizes curation as a diagnostic audit and expands discussion of early/mid-fusion trade-offs. Existing limitations concerning strong visual backbones and the cross-modal performance gap remain.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly states explicitly that the query image is excluded from the search database, which contains geographically matching but visually distinct references. Table 4 clarifies the MixVPR embedding dimension. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, prompts, and code/data access disclosures are retained; construction of the new query-length variants is not explained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and related-work discussion are essentially unchanged. Research positioning becomes more restrained by removing benchmark-priority language and presenting LoRA-MS as an empirical study rather than a novel strategy.

P1.justification: v2 substantially revises the curation and results discussions, reorganizes their presentation, separates limitations from the conclusion, and restructures the supplementary sections. CAT and text-encoder results move into a supplementary results section, references move after the supplement, and cross-modal method terminology changes throughout.

P2.justification: The predominantly two-column document becomes single-column, with extensive table and figure resizing and relocation. v2 adds Table 12 and supplementary Figure 7, redraws the curation diagram, recolors the segmentation visualization, and restructures several tables by shortening headers and removing metric columns.

improvement.justification: The query-length study adds useful evidence about text-only localization, while the revised contribution framing and expanded explanations improve clarity. These are limited gains over otherwise stable methods and headline results. Missing query-generation details, the unexplained 13.2% versus 12.8% BLIP results, and the conflicting backbone caption limit the improvement.
